core_obligations: Produce local data over X (proof lines 6895-6898): for each index i choose syntomic, smooth respectively etale morphisms g_{ij} : V_{ij} -> Y and morphisms V_{ij} x_Y X -> U_i over X such that the base changes form Zariski coverings of U_i, which the cited same-chapter result provides.
Cover the image (proof lines 6899-6900): consequently the union of the images g_{ij}(V_{ij}) contains the closed subset f(X).

Assemble the covering of Y (proof lines 6901-6903): the family of the g_{ij} together with the open immersion Y minus f(X) -> Y is a syntomic, smooth respectively etale covering of Y, and each member either misses f(X) or maps into some U_i, which is the statement.
proof_roadmap: For each member of the given covering of X, lift a Zariski cover of it to morphisms into Y of the same type.
The images of these morphisms cover the closed subset f(X).
Add the open complement of f(X) to obtain a covering of Y.
Each member is either disjoint from f(X) or maps into a member of the original covering.
difficulty_reason: The lemma refines a syntomic, smooth or etale covering of a closed subscheme X of Y to a covering of Y itself, in such a way that each member either misses X or maps into a member of the original covering (statement lines 6885-6892). The proof combines local lifting with a covering of the complement: the cited same-chapter result supplies morphisms to Y whose base changes to X give Zariski covers of the members of the original covering (proof lines 6895-6898), their images cover the closed subset f(X) (proof lines 6899-6900), and the open immersion of the complement Y minus f(X) supplies the remaining member, giving the desired covering of Y (proof lines 6901-6903). The content is the assembly of the two kinds of members. The claim is H2: one application of a lifting result plus one covering of the complement.
